court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: VI Additional Family Court at Chennai, H.M.O.P.No.2559 of 2023
facts_of_case: The respondent filed a divorce petition seeking maintenance for herself and her minor child. The trial court partly allowed the application, directing the petitioner to pay Rs.25,000/- per month as maintenance for the child.

legal_principles.principle: The quantum of interim maintenance ordered by the Family Court is reasonable having regard to the decent income of the respondent.
legal_principles.held: Considering the fact that she is the Government Servant, having decent income, the Family Court rightly came to the conclusion and not ordered any maintenance to her.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking interim maintenance to prove their entitlement.
legal_principles.held: The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that having regard to the income of the petitioner and also the fact that respondent is Government employee, the quantum of interim maintenance fixed by the Family Court is excessive.

outcome.final_order: The Family Court's order was upheld, and the petitioner was directed to pay Rs.25,000/- per month as maintenance for the child.
